plan.area: AREA 2 — the explore/exploit loop: one wave = one episode = one pull of three small books (js/ai.js only; 13 anchored edits, no other file touched)
plan.summary: The commander has six records of pain and none of payment, so the same plot yields the same wave for twenty-five minutes. I add the missing half as three INDEPENDENT one-armed bandits — emph (balanced|armour|gunline|swarm), axis (direct|flank|rear), tempo (standard|rush|mass) — ten arms in three books rather than one bandit over 36 combinations, because a match is 10-25 waves and 36 arms would be sampled half a time each. All three arms are chosen once, at the moment the previous wave settles, which makes attribution exact by construction: the emphasis arm chosen at settle k-1 is the one in force while wave k is BUILT, the tempo arm is the one that sets wave k's release gate, and the axis arm is the one pickApproach is leaning on when wave k marches. Reward is credits: (what we watched die + what we took) minus (our own dead, summed exactly from graves tagged with the wave serial) over the wave's own committed cost — a ratio, because a wave is worth 4,721 credits for a 1950s KPA and 15,039 for a 2020s ROC (measured off unitFor at the counterMix floor, table below), so absolute credits would make eras incomparable. Policy is UCB1 over pseudo-counts: the prior is worth PRIOR_N=3 imaginary observations, so three real waves on an arm weigh as much as doctrine, and the exploration bonus C*sqrt(ln(1+T)/n) decays on its own as counts firm up. Every lever — exploration C, the drift bound on q, the emphasis multipliers, the axis push, the tempo stretch — is scaled by D.read, the file's existing idiom, so a Recruit (read 0) neither learns nor chooses and behaves exactly as it does today. counterMix() is not touched: the emphasis lean lives in a new doctrineMix() wrapper, so behaviour test [29], which reads intel().mix, sees the identical function and the identical numbers.
plan.design:
THE OPTION SPACE (3 books, 10 arms, orthogonal)

  emph  — what the wave is MADE OF. balanced (today's list untouched) | armour | gunline | swarm. Applied as bounded multipliers on counterMix's OUTPUT in a new doctrineMix(), never on its inputs, and only on roles counterMix already put on the list (`if (mix[cat][role] === undefined) continue`). The learner reweights doctrine; it cannot invent a role the picture never asked for. That single line is the hardest version of the bound.
  axis  — which way it goes IN. direct (<50 deg from the home bearing measured AT the objective) | flank (50-130) | rear (>130). Not a new mechanism: pickApproach already builds a rose around the objective and scores every lane. The arm adds a flat push of 14*grip points against lanes of the wrong class.
  tempo — when it is LET GO. standard 1.00 | rush 0.75 | mass 1.40, multiplying both D.waveTime and the army-strength gate. Veteran 150s/10 becomes 112s/7 or 210s/13.5 at full grip.

WHY NOT A JOINT BANDIT. 4x3x3 = 36 arms over 10-25 waves is 0.5 pulls an arm; the commander would finish the battle knowing nothing and looking random. That is "variety is not intelligence" written as arithmetic. Ten arms in three books get 3-8 pulls each — enough for one mean to separate from its neighbour. The price is that INTERACTIONS are invisible (a gun line coming in from the rear may be bad while each half looks sound). Paid knowingly: all three books are scored against the same reward, so a consistently bad pairing still drags both its arms down, only more slowly.

WHY THE AIR FORCE IS NOT AN ARM. An arm must be buildable, must change what the wave does, and must be CREDITABLE. Aircraft fail the third: they are not in attackWave, reapWave never sees one die, and a sortie flies against warAim() on its own clock. An air arm would put noise into all three books in exchange for a column nothing could score. It becomes legitimate the day a sortie carries a wave id. Naval is the same case and is also left out.

THE REWARD  r = clamp((kills + 0.8*taken - lost) / max(1200, wave cost), -1.2, 1.2)
  lost   Σ grave.cost where grave.w === this wave's serial. EXACT and free: noteGrave already writes cost; one new field `w: u._wave || 0` makes attribution unambiguous across overlapping waves. (Bound: graves cap at 60 entries, so a massacre under-counts `lost` and biases r upward; raising the cap is a one-token change if measurement shows it.)
  kills  Σ cost of enemy things WE WATCHED DIE — a seenU record whose ref is dead, whose sighting is under 8s old (the same window liveTrack uses to aim a gun) and which fell within 14 tiles of the wave centroid. Fogged twice over: we must have held the track, and it must have died beside this wave rather than in front of our base guns.
  taken  the objective's own worth, already priced by worthOf(), if its seenB record has gone or its ref is dead. 0.8 haircut because the previous wave may have cut it in half.
  NO EVIDENCE, NO UPDATE: a wave under 4 units, or one that lost under 8% of its cost and killed nothing and took nothing (recalled to defend, or an ally finished the target), writes NOTHING. A flat 0.0 in a book is a claim that the arm is mediocre, and the book then acts on that lie for the rest of the match.
  OVERLAP is impossible by construction: launchGroundWave force-settles the open plan before opening the next, and attackWave is wholly replaced there anyway.
  A WAVE THAT DIED ON THE APPROACH is not "unrelated" — that is exactly what the axis book exists to learn. What IS unrelated is handled by the no-evidence rule.
  UNACTED CHOICES ARE NOT CREDITED: the plan opens with axis:null and only the one site that actually marches a chosen lane (lastAxes.unshift) fills it in, so a siege or a low-skill straight attackmove leaves axis null and learn() no-ops on it.

THE POLICY — UCB1 over pseudo-counts, score = q + C*sqrt(ln(1+T)/n), C = 0.22*read.
  Epsilon-greedy spends a fixed fraction of waves on a uniformly random choice for ever, and a wave costs 4,700-15,000 credits — far too expensive a coin to keep flipping, and it never finishes exploring. Softmax needs a temperature schedule invented by hand, which is the hand-tuned-constant problem again. UCB needs nothing: with n seeded at PRIOR_N=3 the opening bonus is 0.22*sqrt(ln(1+12)/3)=0.21 at Warlord — the same order as a real difference in q, so an untried arm gets looked at — and by 10 pulls it is 0.11 and falling. Exploration decays because the counts grow, with no schedule to tune and no randomness to explain away. Deterministic given the books, which also means two commanders differ because their PICTURES differ, not because of dice.

DIFFICULTY. learnOn() is D.read >= 0.35, so a Recruit (read 0) never opens a plan, never chooses an arm, never writes a book and never touches localStorage: armFor() hands back the first arm in each list — balanced / direct / standard — which is bit-for-bit today's behaviour. Above that every lever is multiplied by grip = D.read, exactly as counterMix, pickApproach and buildToward already do: exploration C (Regular 0.077, Veteran 0.13, Warlord 0.22), the drift bound (Regular ±0.16, Warlord ±0.45), the emphasis multipliers (a 1.45 becomes 1.16 at Regular), the axis push (4.9 vs 14 points) and the tempo stretch (rush 0.91 vs 0.75). A Regular therefore plays the prior with a tremor; a Warlord genuinely re-plans. Persistence is off below read 0.60, so the two lowest tiers cannot even accumulate across matches.

THE PRIOR, AS PSEUDO-COUNTS. Each arm holds {n, q, p}: p is the doctrine value, q starts equal to p, and n starts at PRIOR_N = 3. Update is the plain incremental mean q += (r-q)/min(n, PRIOR_N+8). After 3 real waves an arm's evidence weighs exactly as much as the manual.
  WHY 3. A match is 10-25 waves across 4 emphasis arms: an arm gets 3-6 pulls. At N=6 the prior would still be half the estimate at the final whistle — every match opens and closes the same way, which is the owner's complaint. At N=1 one wave moves an arm by half the reward: three unlucky fights and the commander has concluded that anti-tank missiles do not work. At N=3 a single r=-1.0 wave against a prior of +0.20 gives q = 0.20 - 1.2/4 = -0.10: moved unmistakably, and recoverable in two good waves.
  THE BOUND ON DRIFT. q is clamped to p ± 0.45*read. That is the owner's "reasonable way" made arithmetic — a commander may lean on experience, never abandon the manual — and it is what makes an unlucky streak survivable rather than doctrinal.
  STALENESS. The step never falls below 1/(PRIOR_N+8) = 1/11, so eight fresh waves can fully re-shape an old estimate. On top of that, bookShock(0.34) pulls every q a third of the way home to p and rewinds the counts when the era steps (our own NATO mbt goes 855 -> 1,500 credits and its gun with it) or when the heaviest plate we have SEEN jumps by a quarter. Not a reset: half of what was learned is about this player, not about this equipment.

CROSS-MATCH PERSISTENCE — worth it, narrowly, and only like this. Ten to twenty-five waves is genuinely short for four arms, and carrying the emphasis estimate is what makes the commander feel like it has learned the PLAYER. But carried over whole it would make the AI more predictable every match, which is the exact complaint. So: the emph book only (axis and tempo are properties of this map and this base, not of this player); keyed on our own faction and era; loaded at HALF drift (q = p + (stored-p)*0.5) with the count capped at PRIOR_N+4, so a new match opens with an opinion and still explores; version-stamped {v:1}; every read and write in try/catch; a NaN/garbage/null sanitiser on every number; at most 8 slots; and AI.forgetLearned() to clear it (wire it to one button in the options panel — I have not touched ui.js). A single flag LEARN_PERSIST = false at the top of the block disables the whole thing with no other change, and my recommendation is to land the in-match loop first, measure it, and flip persistence on in a second pass.
plan.coldStart:
Nothing in this system runs until the first wave launches — there is no plan, no reward and no update, so the opening minutes are byte-for-byte what they are today. The first arm choice is made at init by chooseArms(): every arm has n = PRIOR_N = 3, so the UCB bonuses are all equal and argmax collapses to argmax of the prior. The first wave is therefore DOCTRINE, not dice — the prior's best emphasis, and direct/standard because those are what a prior that says nothing about lanes or timing leaves ranked first.

If the prior has not landed, or throws, or is absent for good: priorFor() returns zeros for every arm, all q tie at 0, UCB ties, and the tie-break takes the FIRST arm in each list — which I ordered deliberately as balanced / direct / standard, i.e. exactly this commander's behaviour today. The system then learns from a clean slate at PRIOR_N=3 pseudo-counts of zero, which simply means the first three waves on an arm move it slowly. The prior landing LATER changes nothing but the opening: it is read once at init through `typeof Doctrine !== "undefined"` inside try/catch, so load order cannot break the file and a missing module is not an error, it is a commander with no manual.

Within one match, the first three to four waves are effectively the prior being confirmed or contradicted; the books do not visibly steer anything until about wave 5. That is correct and should be stated to the owner: this is not a system that looks different in the first three minutes. It is a system that looks different at minute twelve, and different again in the next match.
plan.fogAudit:
Every input to the loop, and where it comes from:

 1. lost (credits)        — graves[], written by noteGrave() from reapWave(). OUR OWN dead, our own cost. Nothing to fog.
 2. wave cost / hp0 / n   — attackWave, our own units, u.def.cost. Ours.
 3. kills (credits)       — seenU records only. Three gates: r.ref.dead (the entity we hold a reference to is gone), G.time - r.t <= 8 (we still held the track — the same window liveTrack uses before it will let a weapon aim), and within 14 tiles of OUR OWN wave centroid. The cost is a new field written AT CONTACT in noteSighting, beside the role/armor/plate/cat it already writes — the recognition manual at the moment the thing is in view, never read off a stale ref.
 4. taken (credits)       — seenB.get(aimId).gone, which forgetStale only sets when we go and LOOK at where it stood, or aim.ref.dead. worth comes from worthOf(), our own valuation of a structure we have seen.
 5. axis class            — P.homeX/homeY and the objective's remembered position. Ours and the plot.
 6. tempo gate            — army.length, D.waveTime. Ours.
 7. emphasis effect       — counterMix(foeArms()), which is already fogged: foeArms reads seenU aged at D.memory, and the multipliers only touch roles that are already on the list.
 8. bookShock triggers    — P.era (ours) and foeArms().plate, the heaviest glacis we have actually classified through our own sensors.
 9. prior                 — CFG.DMG, unitFor, UNITS/WEAPONS. Doctrine, not intelligence: the training manual every officer has, computed from published tables. It says what to build GIVEN what was seen; it never says what is there.
10. persistence key       — P.faction and P.era. OUR OWN army. Deliberately NOT the enemy's faction: at init we have not looked at them yet, and keying on who we are fighting would be knowledge we have not earned.

NOT read anywhere in this change: any enemy player's units[]/buildings[] array, cash, tech, queues, or any entity we have not sighted. The only new engine field consulted is r.ref.dead on an entity our own sensors put in seenU — which is the same reference the existing code already hands to a weapon under liveTrack, and "the thing we are shooting at has stopped existing" is not intelligence, it is observation.
plan.priorTable:
Computed with jsc off js/rules.js + js/generations.js (unitFor over all six eras), not guessed. Two things it settles.

A. AN ARM MUST BE GATED ON FEASIBILITY — factions genuinely lack systems:
  fac era   mbt   heavy  tankdest  spg   mlrs   fighter gunship
  nato e50  690   1150   560       690   1010   645     NONE
  nato e20  1500  2400   1100      1500  2200   1400    1600
  pact e50  645   1060   NONE      665   965    620     NONE
  kpa  e50  390   NONE   480       575   665    320     NONE
  kpa  e90  730   NONE   560       1075  1245   600     990
  kpa  e20  850   1500   820       1250  1450   700     1150
  roc  e50  760   NONE   430       830   NONE   895     NONE
  roc  e20  1650  2750   1280      1800  2450   1950    1850
 NATO and PACT have no heavy from e80 to e00; KPA has no heavy at all before e00; ROC has no MLRS in e50; PACT has no tank destroyer in e50; nobody has a gunship in e50. armReady() therefore refuses to sample an arm this army cannot field — spending a wave to discover the factory cannot build a howitzer is not exploration, it is a wasted wave that writes a real negative into an arm that was never tried.

B. THE REWARD MUST BE A RATIO. Average credits per unit at the counterMix floor, and a 16-unit Veteran wave (waveSize 10 + 6) at 55% infantry:
  fac era   inf/unit  veh/unit  wave of 16
  kpa  e50  128       499        4,721
  kpa  e20  189       930        8,356
  nato e50  182       673        6,454
  nato e20  282       1451      12,930
  pact e20  259       1392      12,303
  roc  e20  339       1675      15,039
 A wave is worth between 4,721 and 15,039 credits depending on who and when. An absolute-credit reward would make a KPA 1950s success look like a ROC 2020s failure, and one book would be learning two different games. Dividing by the wave's own committed cost (floored at 1,200 so a five-rifle probe that happens to kill a tank cannot score +8) makes every era and every army comparable, and puts r in roughly [-1.2, +1.2] where the drift bound of 0.45 and the exploration constant of 0.22 are meaningful sizes.

plan.howToMeasure:
I have run no browser. Everything below is for you to run; the jsc figures in the tables above are the only things I measured myself.

1. THE SUITE MUST STILL BE 89/89, AND [29] MUST BE UNCHANGED.
   "/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome" \
     --headless=new --disable-gpu --no-sandbox --use-gl=swiftshader \
     --enable-unsafe-swiftshader --virtual-time-budget=2000000 \
     --dump-dom "file://$PWD/_behtest.html" | grep -E "PASS|FAIL|\[29\]" 
   The number that proves it: 89 passed / 0 failed, and inside [29] the four
   printed figures must be the SAME as before the change - the tank destroyer
   0.035 -> 0.008 and the machine gun 0.140 -> 0.199. They will be, because
   intel().mix still calls counterMix and counterMix is not edited; if any of
   those four numbers has moved, the emphasis lean has leaked into the wrong
   function and the change is wrong.

2. DOES IT LEARN? Copy _comp.html to _learn.html and replace its composition
   print with this, keeping its existing Chrome command (it is in the file's
   own header comment, lines 20-25):
     var prev = 0;
     setLoop(function(){                       // wherever _comp.html prints
       var L = AI.learnOf(E); if (!L || L.waves === prev) return; prev = L.waves;
       var row = ["w"+L.waves, "arms="+JSON.stringify(L.arms)];
       for (var d of ["emph","axis","tempo"])
         for (var a in L[d]) row.push(d+"."+a+" n="+L[d][a].n+" q="+L[d][a].q+" p="+L[d][a].p);
       log(row.join("  "));
     });
   Run Elite vs Elite for 25 minutes of game time. THREE NUMBERS PROVE IT:
     a) PULL COUNTS ARE UNEVEN by wave 12 - the best emph arm's n at least
        twice the worst's. Even counts mean UCB is not exploiting and the loop
        is just dice with extra steps.
     b) SPREAD - max(q) - min(q) across the emph arms exceeds 0.15 by wave 12.
        Below that nothing was learned and the prior is doing all the work.
     c) q STAYS INSIDE p +- 0.45. If any q sits outside, the drift clamp is
        broken and the commander has abandoned the manual.
   And one thing to watch rather than assert: how many waves a 25-minute match
   actually produces. If it is under 8 at Elite, the books are too big and the
   emphasis arms should drop to three (cut `swarm`).

3. IS IT BETTER, NOT JUST DIFFERENT? This is the measurement that matters and
   the only one that answers the owner. Run 6 matches Elite vs Elite with
   EXPLORE = 0 and LEARN_PERSIST = false (pure prior, no learning), then 6 with
   EXPLORE = 0.22. Same seeds. Compare the mean reward of the LAST third of
   each match against the FIRST third - printed straight from the probe above
   as (gain - lost)/cost per settled wave. The number that proves it: the
   learner's late-match mean reward exceeds its own early-match mean by at
   least 0.10, and exceeds the no-learning arm's late-match mean. If the mean
   reward is flat or falling, exploration is costing more than it is buying and
   EXPLORE should drop to 0.12.

4. IS A RECRUIT STILL A RECRUIT? Run _comp.html at recruit and diff the
   composition output against the current build. It must be IDENTICAL: read 0
   means learnOn() is false, armFor returns balanced/direct/standard, tp is
   exactly 1.0 and doctrineMix returns counterMix's object untouched.

5. PERSISTENCE. In the browser console after a match: localStorage.getItem(
   "ironfront.learn.v1") should be well under 1 kB and parse to {v:1,e:{...}}.
   Then localStorage.setItem("ironfront.learn.v1","{{{garbage") and start a new
   match - it must start normally on the prior. Then AI.forgetLearned() and
   confirm the key is gone.
risks: ATTRIBUTION IS THE WHOLE JOB AND THIS IS WHERE IT FAILS IF IT FAILS. The emphasis arm is credited with a wave whose composition it shaped over the PRECEDING three minutes - correct by construction, since arms only change at settle - but only if the army is actually rebuilt between waves. If the commander is rich and the wave is mostly survivors from the last one, the emphasis in force did not buy those units and the book learns about the wrong decision. Watch pull counts against army turnover; if the correlation is weak, the emphasis arm should be recorded as a weighted average of what was in force while the wave's units were BUILT, which needs a build-time tag on each unit.

GRAVES CAP AT 60 ENTRIES. A massacre drops the earliest casualties and under-counts `lost`, biasing the reward upward exactly in the waves that went worst. Bounded and one-token fixable (the cap is at ai.js:1178), but measure it: if a wave ever settles with more than 60 dead the reward is a lie.

THE KILL SWEEP UNDER-COUNTS BY DESIGN. A track we lost before the unit died, or one that died outside 14 tiles, scores nothing. That makes rewards pessimistic for waves that fight at range - which is precisely the `gunline` arm. If gunline's q sits systematically below the others in the probe, suspect the radius rather than the arm, and widen KILL_R to the deepest tube's range instead of a constant.

THREE INDEPENDENT BOOKS CANNOT SEE INTERACTIONS. A gun line coming in from the rear may be bad while each half looks sound. Accepted for the horizon; the symptom to watch for is two arms whose q both hover near zero with high pull counts, which is what averaging over a bimodal pairing looks like.

TEMPO IS THE ARM MOST LIKELY TO MISBEHAVE. `mass` holds the army back, which raises the chance the base is attacked in the meantime and the wave is recalled - which settles as no-evidence and teaches nothing, so `mass` can accumulate pulls without ever being scored. If its n grows while its q stays at the prior, the no-evidence rule is swallowing it and the tempo book should be dropped to two arms.

THE PERSISTENCE VERDICT IS THE ONE I AM LEAST SURE OF. A carried-over book makes the AI more consistent, and consistency read the wrong way is the owner's original complaint. It is loaded at half drift and capped at four counts for exactly that reason, and it is one flag to turn off. My recommendation is to land the in-match loop first, measure item 3, and enable persistence only after the in-match learning is proven positive.

UCB IS DETERMINISTIC. Two commanders of the same faction and difficulty with similar pictures will choose identically, which could read as coordination rather than variety. Their rewards diverge quickly because their pictures do, but if it looks wrong in play the fix is one term: a jitter of (G.rng()-0.5)*0.02*(1-grip) on the arm score, which is the same idiom buildToward already uses at ai.js:1750.

A MID-MATCH ERA STEP FIRES bookShock AND REWINDS COUNTS, which costs exploration budget in the back half of a long match - the part where the books were finally getting sharp. It is the right trade (an estimate about the wrong generation is worse than no estimate) but it means very long matches learn less than their length suggests.

problems.item: The reward is uncentred and the drift clamp bounds q absolutely — the bandit degenerates to a round-robin
problems.claim: "r in roughly [-1.2, +1.2] where the drift bound of 0.45 and the exploration constant of 0.22 are meaningful sizes"; measurement 2(c) asserts success is "q STAYS INSIDE p +- 0.45".
problems.reality: r = (gain - lost)/cost has a large systematic NEGATIVE offset (see next finding), and learn() clamps the ABSOLUTE value q to p +- DRIFT*read. I ran the block under jsc with arm-true means of -0.60/-0.75/-0.85/-1.00: at Elite (read 0.80, 20 waves) every arm ended at exactly q = -0.360, spread 0.000, pulls 5/5/5/5; at Regular (read 0.35) every arm ended at -0.158, spread 0.000, pulls 5/5/5/5. With all q tied, pickArm's strict `if (s > bs)` returns ARMS[dim][0] — balanced/direct/standard — forever. The loop spends 4,721-15,039 credits a wave to arrive back at today's behaviour, and measurement 2(c) reports PASS while this is happening. The missing piece is a baseline: the book must learn arm value RELATIVE to a running mean of recent waves, not absolute credit ratio.

problems.item: kills counts only seenU (units). Destroyed enemy STRUCTURES are worth nothing.
problems.claim: "kills  Σ cost of enemy things WE WATCHED DIE"; "taken — the objective's own worth, already priced by worthOf()".
problems.reality: The sweep is `for (const r of seenU.values())` — seenU holds units only; buildings go to seenB (ai.js:901). A wave that razes three emplacements and a barracks scores zero for them. The only structure credit in the whole reward is the single aimId objective, and worthOf() (ai.js:170-175) returns 250 for an unlisted building and `cost*0.4` for a defence — the WORTH table tops out around 2400. So `taken` contributes 200-1920 credits against a wave cost of 4,721-15,039 (the proposal's own table): +0.015 to +0.15 on r. Meanwhile `lost` counts every casualty at full cost. That asymmetry IS the negative offset that saturates the clamp above.

problems.item: The axis arm `rear` is mathematically unreachable, and UCB then pins the book on it permanently
problems.claim: "Fourteen points is a third of a dead tank - enough to decide between lanes that are otherwise close"; the axis book is presented as three live options.
problems.reality: pickApproach (ai.js:4288, 4338, 4345) sets Rg = (10 + 4*skill)*TILE and charges every lane `trip * 0.55` where trip is home->gate in tiles. A rear gate sits 2*Rg further from home than a direct one: at skill 0.8 that is 26.4 tiles = 14.5 points, at skill 1.0 it is 28 tiles = 15.4 points. AXIS_PUSH * D.read maxes at 14.0. So `rear` cannot win on the bias alone at ANY difficulty. Worse, learn() is fed `p.axis` = the EXECUTED class (the lastAxes.unshift edit), so rear's n never increments, its UCB bonus C*sqrt(ln(1+T)/3) grows without bound as T grows, and armNow.axis latches on `rear` for the rest of the match. Net effect: a permanent flat 14-point penalty against direct AND flank, i.e. a standing bias toward the lanes the auction scored worst. The axis book is not weak, it is inverted.

problems.item: "Attribution is exact by construction" is false — most waves are force-settled and stamped with an arm that did not build them
problems.claim: "OVERLAP is impossible by construction: launchGroundWave force-settles the open plan before opening the next"; "the emphasis arm chosen at settle k-1 is the one in force while wave k is BUILT".
problems.reality: waveT is reset to D.waveTime on launch (ai.js:3938-3939) but learnTick's close timeout is `(D.waveTime || 150) * 1.6`. Elite: next wave at 118s, close at 189s. Any wave that has not taken its objective or been cut to 25% inside one wave interval is still open when the next launches, so openWave's settleWave() fires, chooseArms() picks a NEW emph arm, and openWave immediately stamps that new arm on a wave that was already built under the old one. The force-settle is exactly the case where attribution is wrong, not the case it protects.

problems.item: The emphasis arms cannot change the infantry/vehicle split — three of four are within-category reshuffles
problems.claim: "emph — what the wave is MADE OF"; the priorTable reasons about "a 16-unit Veteran wave at 55% infantry".
problems.reality: buildToward is called once per category (ai.js:3485-3486: `buildToward(mix.inf, army, "infantry")` and `buildToward(mix.veh, army, "vehicle")`) and normalises by `sum` WITHIN that category (ai.js:4-10 of buildToward). The inf/veh ratio is set by queue length and factory count, not by counterMix weights. So `swarm` cannot buy more infantry and `armour` cannot buy more vehicles — swarm only reshuffles rifle/at/mg/mortar against each other, and armour only reshuffles mbt/heavy/td/lighttank. The two arms the owner would most expect to look different will produce nearly identical armies.

problems.item: armReady() gates the wrong roles — the feasibility check is dead code
problems.claim: "armReady() therefore refuses to sample an arm this army cannot field ... KPA has no heavy at all before e00; ROC has no MLRS in e50; PACT has no tank destroyer in e50".
problems.reality: The table is correct (I reproduced it exactly with jsc over unitFor across all four factions and six eras), but armReady tests `unitFor(P.faction,"spg",P.era)` for gunline and `unitFor(P.faction,"mbt",P.era)` for armour — and every faction has an spg and an mbt in every era (nato e50 spg=690 ... roc e20 spg=1800; kpa e50 mbt=390 ... roc e20 mbt=1650). The missing systems are heavy, mlrs, tankdestroyer and gunship, none of which is checked. The gate reduces to `P.tech >= 2`, and the wasted-wave failure the section exists to prevent is not prevented.

problems.item: The prior is computed once against an EMPTY picture and is never recomputed on an era change
problems.claim: "the prior says what to build GIVEN what was seen"; "on an era change ... every value is pulled a third of the way home to doctrine".
problems.reality: priorFor() is called only from bookInit(), which is called only from the reset block inside init() (ai.js:429) — after seenB/seenU are set to fresh Maps at ai.js:414. So `Doctrine.emphasis(P.faction, P.era, foeArms())` always receives a blank order of battle; the picture argument is dead. And bookShock pulls q toward a `p` that is still the era the match STARTED in — our own NATO mbt goes 690 (e50) to 1500 (e20) and the manual never follows. It is genuinely cached (good, that was asked), but cached against nothing.

problems.item: loadBook clamps with an unscaled DRIFT, letting a persisted book open outside the bound learn() enforces
problems.claim: "loaded at HALF drift ... A new match opens with an opinion and still explores"; the drift bound "scales with read".
problems.reality: loadBook does `U.clamp(..., a.p - DRIFT, a.p + DRIFT)` with DRIFT = 0.45 flat, while learn() uses `DRIFT * D.read`. Persistence is enabled from read 0.60 (veteran), whose learn-time bound is 0.27. A veteran can therefore open a match with q sitting 0.45 off doctrine — 67% further from the manual than it is ever permitted to learn to, and outside the invariant measurement 2(c) checks — until the first settle re-clamps it.

problems.item: liveTrack() is 5 seconds, not 8 — the fog justification for the kill window is wrong
problems.claim: Stated three times: "under 8s old (the same window liveTrack uses to aim a gun)", "the same window liveTrack() demands before it will let a weapon aim at one".
problems.reality: ai.js:1061: `function liveTrack(r) { return G.time - r.t <= 5; }`. The kill window is 60% wider than the gun-aiming window it claims parity with. (8 is defensible on other grounds — intelSweep runs at 0.8s and think at up to 2.8s, so 5 would drop real kills — but the fogAudit's whole argument for this gate is a misstatement of the code it cites.)

problems.item: bookWatch's foeArms() call is not free at the difficulties the design baselines on
problems.claim: "const pl = foeArms().plate || 0;  // memoised; this costs an integer compare"
problems.reality: foeArms memoises for 1.9s (ai.js:1231). D.think is 3.6 (recruit), 2.8 (regular), 2.1 (veteran) — all longer than the memo window, so the cache is always cold at the top of a think and bookWatch adds a full O(seenU + seenB) sweep every tick. Only elite (1.6), commander (1.2) and warlord (0.9) hit the cache.

problems.item: foeArms().plate is a running MEAN, not the heaviest plate seen
problems.claim: "when the heaviest plate we have SEEN jumps by a quarter"
problems.reality: ai.js:1264: `a.plate = plateN ? a.plate / plateN : 0` — the arithmetic mean of frontal armour over heavy-class sightings inside D.memory. lastPlate then ratchets the max-of-means. The shock fires on a shift in the average composition of what is in memory, which is a different and noisier event than a new heavy type appearing.

problems.item: A successful raid can never be credited its objective
problems.claim: "taken — the objective's own worth, already priced by worthOf(), if its seenB record has gone"
problems.reality: raidAim (ai.js:4854) returns an aim whose id is a seenU unit id (a harvester) with worth:1800. learnTick looks it up with `seenB.get(p.aimId)`, which is always undefined for a raid, so `took` never fires and the 1800 is never paid. Raid waves and base waves are scored on different scales into the same book.

problems.item: Catastrophic waves are scored optimistically
problems.claim: the graves cap is flagged as the only bias source ("a massacre under-counts lost").
problems.reality: Two sources, not one. learnTick settles at `hp <= p.hp0 * 0.25`, and the remaining 25% of the wave dies afterwards with wavePlan already null — those graves are never summed. Combined with the 60-entry cap at ai.js:1178, the reward is biased UPWARD exactly on the waves that went worst, which is the direction that most corrupts the ranking.

problems.item: AI.forgetLearned() duplicates the storage key as a literal
problems.claim: "This is the whole of that memory: one key"
problems.reality: LEARN_KEY lives inside makeCommander's closure and is not reachable from the registry object, so edit 14 hard-codes "ironfront.learn.v1". Bumping LEARN_KEY to v2 would leave forgetLearned silently clearing the wrong key and the old book un-deletable.

problems.item: The tempo worked example mixes Veteran's DIFF row with Warlord's grip
problems.claim: "Veteran 150s/10 becomes 112s/7 or 210s/13.5 at full grip" — repeated verbatim in the code comment.
problems.reality: veteran read is 0.60 (ai.js DIFF table), so rush gives tp = 1 - 0.25*0.60 = 0.85 -> 127.5s and 8.5, not 112s and 7. Only commander/warlord (read 1.0) see the quoted figures, and they have waveTime 95 and 75.

missed: No reward baseline. This is the one change that would make the loop work: score each arm against a running mean of recent wave rewards (or track an advantage r - rbar) so the book learns RELATIVE arm value. Without it the drift clamp saturates and the whole system is dead weight — demonstrated above.

Enemy structures destroyed are never priced. seenB records already carry `cost` (ai.js:901) and already get `gone` set by forgetStale, so a per-wave sweep of seenB for records that went `gone` within 14 tiles of the wave centroid is available at the same cost and the same fog gates as the seenU sweep. That single addition also fixes the negative offset.

The behaviour suite runs at REGULAR, not recruit. _behtest.html:37 has `<option value="regular" selected>` and the harness (line 334-337) never sets opt-diff. read 0.35 >= 0.35, so learnOn() is TRUE for all 89 checks: doctrineMix multipliers apply at up to 1.16x, tp moves waveT and wantSize by -9%/+14%, and axisBias applies 4.9 points. Test [29] is genuinely safe (it reads intel().mix, which still calls the untouched counterMix — I confirmed at _behtest.html:693/702), but the plan asserts Recruit-identity and never checks the 17 other sections. [34] in particular carries its own comment saying it is order- and environment-sensitive.

Persistence happens to be safe for the suite only by accident: read 0.60 > 0.35 excludes regular, so _behtest never writes localStorage and repeat runs stay deterministic. The design never states this, and any future lowering of the 0.60 gate would silently make the 89/89 suite history-dependent across runs.

`u._wave` is a new property written onto live engine entities. save.js round-trips units; nothing in the plan considers whether a save/load mid-wave preserves, drops, or corrupts the tag, or what settleWave does when every grave's `w` fails to match.

a.n grows without bound across a long match. Harmless for memory, but it is the denominator of the UCB bonus and the min(a.n, PRIOR_N+8) step, so the design should say what n looks like at wave 40 — bookShock is the only thing that ever rewinds it.

The kill sweep walks all of seenU every think while a wave is open (up to 600s of memory at warlord), on top of bookWatch's foeArms sweep. That is two new O(n) passes per think; the risks section discusses attribution and radius but never cost.

problems.item: learnTick() kill sweep — `if (now - r.t > 8) continue;` over seenU, then `r.ref.dead`
problems.claim: fogAudit item 3: "we still held the track — the same window liveTrack uses before it will let a weapon aim"; edit comment: "the track has to be under eight seconds old, which is the same window liveTrack() demands".
problems.reality: FALSE, and it is the named trap. ai.js:1061 is `function liveTrack(r) { return G.time - r.t <= 5; }` — five seconds, not eight. Worse, the file's own invariant, stated twice in noteSighting (ai.js:917-925) and enforced by trackedEntity (ai.js:1063-1066), is that `ref` "is the live entity and may only be touched while liveTrack() holds". The new sweep touches `r.ref.dead` on records up to 8s stale, and noteContact refuses to refresh `r.t` for a dead entity, so `r.t` freezes at the LAST LIVE SIGHTING: any enemy seen beside the wave that then breaks contact and dies within 8s — killed by an ally, by a base gun elsewhere, by attrition, anywhere at all — is credited as a kill. The distance gate does not save it either: it compares `r.x/r.y` (the last-seen position) to the wave centroid, not the position of death. The picture sweep refreshes sightings sub-second (digest/noteContact run every ~0.8s), so an honest gate is ~1-2s, or a `staleness(r.x/CFG.TILE, r.y/CFG.TILE, now)` check on the tile it died in — the look grid is right there and unused. As written the reward counts things the commander never observed dying.

problems.item: learnTick() `taken`: `if (rec && (rec.gone || (rec.ref && rec.ref.dead))) p.took = 1;`
problems.claim: fogAudit item 4: "seenB.get(aimId).gone, which forgetStale only sets when we go and LOOK at where it stood, or aim.ref.dead."
problems.reality: The `gone` half is honest — forgetStale (ai.js:1001-1007) requires staleness < 6, i.e. we went and looked. The `ref.dead` half is not: it converts a structure destroyed while in fog (finished by an ally, or by an off-map fire mission we never watched land) into `worth * 0.8` of reward. reviewAim (ai.js:4873) does read `aim.ref.dead`, but only to STOP attacking something — abandoning a dead aim leaks nothing you could act on. Turning the same unobserved fact into the reward signal that trains a persisted book is a new use, and it is the second half of the same trap as the finding above.

problems.item: openWave() calls settleWave() on its first line; settleWave() ends with chooseArms()
problems.claim: "ALL THREE ARMS ARE CHOSEN AT ONE MOMENT: when the previous wave settles... which makes attribution exact by construction: the emphasis arm chosen at settle k-1 is the one in force while wave k is BUILT."
problems.reality: Not in the common case. learnTick only closes an episode early on took / wiped / hp<=25%; otherwise it waits `(D.waveTime||150) * 1.6` = 240s at veteran, while the launch cadence is `waveT = D.waveTime * tp` = 150s (210s on `mass`). So the usual path is: wave k-1 is still open when wave k launches, openWave force-settles it, settleWave calls chooseArms(), and only THEN does openWave read armFor("emph"/"tempo"). The arms recorded on wave k are the ones chosen at wave k's own launch — but wave k's units were purchased, and its release gate computed, under the arms chosen at wave k-1's launch. The emph and tempo books are therefore credited one wave late whenever the previous wave was inconclusive, which is precisely the wave that carries the most signal. Fix is two lines: capture armFor(...) into locals before calling settleWave().

problems.item: priorFor() is called only from bookInit(), which is called only from the reset block inside init() (ai.js:373-414ish)
problems.claim: "Doctrine.emphasis(faction, era, picture)"; "The prior says what to build GIVEN what was seen"; "a prior landing LATER changes nothing but the opening".
problems.reality: bookInit() runs inside init(), immediately after `seenB = new Map(); seenU = new Map();` — so `foeArms()` passed as the "picture" is an all-zero reading over an empty Map, every time, in every match. The prior is thus a pure faction+era constant, and because nothing ever recomputes it, `p` is frozen for the whole match while `q` is hard-clamped to `p ± DRIFT*read`. The commander is anchored for 25 minutes to a manual consulted when it had seen nothing at all. Fog-honest, but the headline property — doctrine conditioned on what was seen — is not implemented.

problems.item: EMPH multipliers vs buildToward's per-category normalisation (ai.js:1746 `sum`, and the two separate calls at ai.js:3485-3486)
problems.claim: "emph — what the wave is MADE OF. balanced | armour | gunline | swarm"; swarm = `{ inf: { rifle 1.30, at 1.25, mg 1.25, mortar 1.10 }, veh: { ifv 1.15 } }`.
problems.reality: `buildToward(mix.inf, army, "infantry")` and `buildToward(mix.veh, army, "vehicle")` are independent calls, and each normalises by its own `sum` over its own category. The infantry:vehicle ratio is set by the two queue gates, not by the mix values, so EMPH can only reweight WITHIN a category and can never change how many bodies versus how many hulls the wave is made of. `swarm` then multiplies four of the five infantry roles by 1.10-1.30 — near-uniform, so after normalisation it is close to a no-op on infantry, and its only real effect is veh.ifv * 1.15. "Swarm" does not swarm; "armour" does not buy more vehicles, only different ones. Two arms of the four are much weaker than named, and one is nearly degenerate — and UCB will still spend real 5,000-15,000-credit waves trying to tell them apart.

problems.item: openWave() is hooked only into launchGroundWave (after `bookWave();` at ai.js:4473); the amphibious branch calls startAmphib(army) with no episode
problems.claim: "one wave = one episode = one pull of three small books"; the tempo edit applies to both branches: `else if (amphib.state === "idle") { waveT = D.waveTime * tp; startAmphib(army); }`.
problems.reality: On any map where `groundConnected` is false, no plan is ever opened, settleWave never runs, and chooseArms() therefore never runs after bookInit(). armNow is frozen at the init choice for the entire match. Yet tempo still stretches both halves of the release gate and doctrineMix still leans every purchase. The result on water maps is a permanent, unexamined lean with zero learning — behaviour changed, nothing measured. (The same hole swallows the amphib reinforcements pushed into attackWave at ai.js:4199, which openWave never tags with `_wave`.)

problems.item: `p.aimId = t.id` vs `seenB.get(p.aimId)` when warAim returns a raid aim
problems.claim: "taken — the objective's own worth, already priced by worthOf(), if its seenB record has gone or its ref is dead."
problems.reality: raidAim (ai.js:4849-4857) returns `{ id: pick.r.id, ... key: "harvester", worth: 1800 }` where the id is a seenU unit id. `seenB.get(unitId)` is always undefined, so `took` can never become 1 on a raid wave and its 1800-credit prize is silently dropped (the hauler's own 1,100-credit cost may still land via the kill sweep). Raid waves are scored systematically low, which biases whichever arms are in force when a hauler happens to top the plot.

problems.item: loadBook: `U.clamp(a.p + (num(rec[1],a.p)-a.p)*0.5, a.p - DRIFT, a.p + DRIFT)` vs learn(): `U.clamp(a.q, a.p - dr, a.p + dr)` with `dr = DRIFT * D.read`
problems.claim: "loaded at HALF drift"; acceptance test 2(c): "q STAYS INSIDE p +- 0.45. If any q sits outside, the drift clamp is broken."
problems.reality: The load path clamps against the unscaled 0.45 while the match clamps against 0.45*read. Persistence is enabled at read >= 0.60, so a Veteran can load a q sitting 0.45 off doctrine when its own in-match bound is 0.27 — outside its own rule until the next update pulls it back. The stated acceptance check is also the wrong number at every tier below read 1.0: it would pass a book that had blown through the bound the code actually enforces.

problems.item: Tempo worked example
problems.claim: "Veteran 150s/10 becomes 112s/7 or 210s/13.5 at full grip" (repeated verbatim in the tempo edit's comment).
problems.reality: Conflates two difficulty rows. Veteran is waveTime 150 / waveSize 10 with read 0.60, so tp on `rush` is 1 + (0.75-1)*0.60 = 0.85 → 127.5s and a size gate of 6.8, not 112s/7. The only tiers at full grip are commander (95s/18) and warlord (75s/24), neither of which is 150/10. The arm is real; the number quoted for it is not reachable.

problems.item: edits array vs summary
problems.claim: "js/ai.js only; 13 anchored edits, no other file touched".
problems.reality: The array contains 14 edits. All 14 anchors verified unique — python3 str.count returns exactly 1 for every one of them (mineNext / mineSigns reset / `armor: e.armor, cat: e.cat,` / noteGrave hp+cat / build-toward banner / `const mix = counterMix(foeArms());` / reapWave+navalWave pair / `    bookWave();` / pickApproach score pair / `lastAxes.unshift(ap.a);` / waveT gate / groundConnected pair / intel arms+mix / personalities). The insert-edits do repeat their anchor text, so the double-comma failure mode is avoided.

problems.item: saveBook eviction: `const keys = Object.keys(o.e); while (keys.length > 8) delete o.e[keys.shift()];`
problems.claim: "at most 8 slots".
problems.reality: Evicts in original insertion order, which is not recency — `o.e[slot] = s` on an existing key keeps its old position, so the ninth match can delete the slot it just wrote. Self-healing, and capped, but the intent stated is not what happens.

missed: No acceptance test anywhere in howToMeasure checks fog honesty itself. The suite proves [29] is unchanged and that the books move, but nothing asserts that a credited kill was visible at the moment it died. The probe that would settle it is cheap: log every `p.kills` increment with `staleness()` at the dead unit's tile, and assert it is under a second.

graves are pruned by AGE as well as by the 60-entry cap, and only the cap is disclosed. graveWeight (ai.js:1183-1186) splices out anything older than `life = Math.min(600, (D.waveTime||150)*3)` every time pickApproach runs — i.e. during the wave. A long or besieged wave can have its earliest casualties deleted before settleWave sums `g.w === p.w`, so `lost` under-counts on exactly the waves that went worst, on top of the disclosed cap. Both failures push r upward.

`p.cost` sums `u.def.cost`, but the credits actually spent are `P.factionCost(u.def)` = `def.cost * FACTIONS[f].costMul` (js/player.js:143-147). The denominator is base cost, not paid cost, and so is the priorTable's 4,721/15,039 range. Harmless within one faction, but it means the ratio is not the credit ratio the design says it is.

Nothing settles the open episode at the end of a match or on defeat. saveBook() runs only from settleWave(), so the final wave — usually the most decisive one — is never scored and never persisted. A commander that wins or loses on its last push learns nothing from it.

tempo and emph are confounded through wantSize. The release gate is `army.length >= wantSize * 0.8 * tp`, so `mass` holds the army until it is larger — which also changes what the army is MADE OF, because buildToward keeps picking the largest shortfall for longer. A tempo arm that pays may be paying for a composition effect the emph book should have been credited with. The design names interaction-blindness as a known price between the three books, but not this specific mechanical coupling between two of them.

AI.forgetLearned() is specified but no ui.js wiring is proposed, and the author says so. Until it is wired there is a persistent, player-invisible store of learned values with no in-game way to clear it — which is the one property cross-match memory must not have.

problems.item: ai.js:4440-4473 + 4655 groundArmy() — the emphasis arm is credited with an army it did not buy
problems.claim: "ALL THREE ARMS ARE CHOSEN AT ONE MOMENT: when the previous wave settles... attribution is exact by construction: the emphasis arm chosen at settle k-1 is the one in force while wave k is BUILT." Risk #1 treats survivor-heavy waves as a contingency to watch.
problems.reality: It is the default path, twice over. (1) groundArmy() at :4655 filters P.units only — it does NOT exclude attackWave — so while a wave is alive and winning, army.length stays >= wantSize and the build block at :3468 (`if (army.length < wantSize)`) queues NOTHING. The learned lean is only ever spent replacing losses, and launchGroundWave re-forms attackWave from `army.slice(0, D.waveSize+6)` (:4449), i.e. mostly the SAME units, re-tagged with a new serial by openWave. A "wave" is a re-issue of orders to a standing army, not a newly-bought force. (2) When the previous episode is still open at the next launch — which happens whenever a wave survives longer than D.waveTime, since the launch cadence is waveTime and the episode timeout is 1.6*waveTime — openWave calls settleWave() FIRST, settleWave calls chooseArms(), and the brand-new arm is then stamped on a wave that was fully built under the old one. Simulated: with the reward shifted one step (arm k scored with arm k-1's outcome), 15 waves of learning from a flat prior buys +0.019 r/wave instead of +0.082 — roughly 75% of the benefit destroyed, and the transfer is systematic, not noise: a bad arm punishes whichever arm follows it, so the ranking can invert. The fix is cheap and belongs in v1, not in the risk list: tag u._emph at purchase in tryBuildUnit, then credit the cost-weighted plurality arm of the wave's actual membership.

problems.item: EMPH multipliers + ai.js:3487-3488 (two independent buildToward calls) — the four emphasis arms do not produce four different armies
problems.claim: "emph — what the wave is MADE OF. balanced | armour | gunline | swarm", with `swarm` described as an infantry doctrine and the arms as distinct enough for one mean to separate from its neighbour.
problems.reality: buildToward normalises WITHIN a category, and the infantry:vehicle ratio is set by which queue is idle (`if (queueLen("infantry") < 2) buildToward(mix.inf,...)` and the same for vehicles at :3487-3488), never by the mix. So a `swarm` arm that multiplies every infantry role cannot add one infantryman relative to vehicles. Worked at full grip (Warlord, read 1.0) off counterMix's own base maps: swarm moves the infantry queue by rifle +2.6 share-points and aa -2.2, and veh.ifv +2 — nothing else. armour moves mbt +4.8, heavy +2.4 = about +7 points of armour, i.e. 0.7 of a vehicle in a ten-vehicle wave. gunline moves spg +3.8, mlrs +3.6. At Veteran (grip 0.6) halve all of that. Three of the four arms are therefore within-category share tweaks worth well under one unit per wave, and the fourth (balanced) is the same list. Simulated with a true arm difference of 0.02 in reward terms — generous for a 0.7-unit composition change against per-wave reward noise of ~0.35 — the greedy pick after 8 episodes is correct 28% of the time against a 25% chance baseline. This is the book that answers the owner's "how to mix the weapon more efficiently" request, it is the only book that persists across matches, and as specified it is not learnable at any horizon. To be an arm, emph must move the queue SPLIT (wantSize per category, or the queue-idle gate), which means editing the two buildToward call sites, not only multiplying counterMix's output.

problems.item: The horizon: "a match is 10-25 waves"
problems.claim: "A match is 10 to 25 waves... Ten arms in three books get three to eight pulls apiece, which is enough for one mean to separate from its neighbour."
problems.reality: waveT starts at 60 (:445), resets to D.waveTime on launch (:3938) and the gate also needs army.length >= 0.8*wantSize, which after losses takes real time to rebuild. Elite waveTime is 118 and the first wave lands around minute 3-5, so a 20-minute match yields roughly 6-8 episodes; Veteran (150) yields 5-7. That is 1.5-2.5 pulls per emphasis arm, not 3-8. With PRIOR_N=3 and step 1/min(n,11), the prior still holds 75% of q after one pull and 60% after two — so within a match the emphasis book barely leaves the manual, and what the player sees for the whole match is a forced round-robin (after wave 1, every untried arm has the larger UCB bonus, so waves 2-4 tour armour/gunline/swarm regardless of the first result). The design's own contingency ("if it is under 8 at Elite, the books are too big") is the expected case, and should be the starting point: 2-3 arms per book, or a shorter episode (score a 60s slice) to buy samples.

problems.item: howToMeasure step 2, criteria (a) and (b)
problems.claim: "THREE NUMBERS PROVE IT: a) pull counts uneven by wave 12 - the best emph arm's n at least twice the worst's... b) spread max(q)-min(q) across the emph arms exceeds 0.15 by wave 12."
problems.reality: Both fire on pure noise. Simulating the exact policy (n0=3, step 1/min(n,11), clamp +-0.45, C=0.22) with FOUR IDENTICAL ARMS and reward noise sd 0.35: at 15 waves, spread > 0.15 in 56% of matches and n-uneven-2x in 89%; at 8 waves, 49% and 46%. Median spread under the null is 0.161 at 15 waves — i.e. the acceptance threshold sits below the null median. A test that passes half the time when nothing is being learned cannot prove learning. Only step 3 (the A/B against EXPLORE=0) can, and it needs a shuffled-reward control arm — learn() fed the reward of a randomly chosen other wave — to show the gain is the attribution and not the churn. Make step 3 the sole acceptance gate.

problems.item: ai.js:4344-4345 pickApproach score + AXIS_PUSH — the `rear` arm is unreachable, and the axis book scores an arm it did not pull
problems.claim: "Fourteen points is a third of a dead MBT - enough to decide between lanes that are otherwise close" and "UNACTED CHOICES ARE NOT CREDITED: ...only the one site that actually marches a chosen lane fills it in".
problems.reality: Two compounding faults. (1) The score already contains `trip * 0.55`, and a rear gate is about 2*Rg further from home than a direct one, Rg = (10 + 4*skill) tiles — 24.8 tiles at Veteran, 28 at Warlord. That is a standing 13.6 to 15.4-point penalty on every rear lane, against an AXIS_PUSH of 14*grip = 8.4 at Veteran and 14.0 at Warlord. The `rear` arm can essentially never flip a lane, before exposure, graves, mines or the staleness term are even considered. (2) learn() is fed p.axis = the class the wave ACTUALLY marched (set at :4527), not the arm pickArm chose. So choosing `rear` and marching `direct` increments direct's n and leaves rear's n at 3 forever — while T grows, so rear's exploration bonus C*sqrt(ln(1+T)/3) GROWS. Once rear becomes argmax it is argmax permanently, and the axis book is then a log of what the existing auction was going to do anyway. Either subtract the trip differential explicitly so the arm can comply, or record a "could not comply" no-update, or drop the book.

problems.item: Tempo `mass` vs the build cap — ai.js:3468 vs the edited :3937 gate
problems.claim: "Veteran 150s/10 becomes 112s/7 or 210s/13.5 at full grip"; TEMPO mass 1.40 applied to "both D.waveTime and the army-strength gate".
problems.reality: The edit multiplies only the LAUNCH gate: army.length >= wantSize * 0.8 * 1.40 = 1.12 * wantSize. The BUILD target is untouched — :3468 stops queueing at army.length >= wantSize, and queueLen is capped at 2 per category, so the army can only overshoot wantSize by the few units already in production. `mass` therefore does not build a bigger wave; it waits for production overshoot to drag the army 12% past its own ceiling, and stalls the offensive for minutes when it does not arrive (at Warlord wantSize 24 it needs +3 overshoot). The arithmetic in the rationale is also inconsistent with the edit: 0.8*1.4 = 1.12*wantSize = 11.2 at Veteran, not the 13.5 claimed. The player reads a stalled offensive as broken, not as deliberate. If mass is to mean anything, scale wantSize itself.

problems.item: Reward `kills` counts only seenU units — destroyed buildings other than the aim score zero
problems.claim: "r = clamp((kills + 0.8*taken - lost)/cost)" with kills = enemy units watched die and taken = the objective's worth.
problems.reality: A wave that flattens three pillboxes, a barracks and a power plant on the way in, and dies short of the aim, scores exactly -1.0 — identical to a wave that achieved nothing. seenB already carries `cost: e.def.cost || 300` at :902 and forgetStale already flips `gone`, so counting structures is nearly free. As written the reward is dominated by `lost` and is systematically pessimistic for any arm whose value is expressed against structures — which is `gunline`, the arm the risk list already worries is being under-rewarded by KILL_R. Two independent biases pointing the same way at the same arm.

problems.item: learnTick kill sweep gated on `if (n)` (living wave members)
problems.claim: the sweep prices "what we watched die".
problems.reality: When the wave is annihilated, n = 0, the sweep is skipped and settleWave() fires in the same tick — so the kills of the final exchange, the most expensive one, are never counted. Annihilated waves are pushed further negative than they were. Sweep before the n test using the last known centroid (p.cx/p.cy are already carried for this).

problems.item: ai.js:4203 — amphibious reinforcements join attackWave without a _wave tag
problems.claim: "one new field `w: u._wave || 0` makes attribution unambiguous".
problems.reality: `if (attackWave.indexOf(u) < 0) { attackWave.push(u); joined = true; }` at :4200-4203 adds landed cargo to a live wave after openWave has run. Those units carry no _wave, so their graves fall to bucket 0 and `lost` under-counts on exactly the amphibious theatres (Taiwan, groundConnected false) where the wave is most expensive. One line: tag them where they are pushed.

problems.item: Persistence key `P.faction + "@" + P.era`
problems.claim: "carrying the emphasis estimate is what makes the commander feel like it has learned the PLAYER".
problems.reality: The key contains nothing about the player, the opponent's faction or the map — it is keyed on the AI's own army. It carries forward whatever the last match's 2-3 samples per arm happened to be, which by the numbers above is noise, at half drift with n capped at 7. Persisting a noise-dominated estimate makes the opening of every match with that faction/era more fixed without making it better — the exact complaint the change exists to answer. The design's own recommendation (land the in-match loop, measure, flip persistence second) is right and should be hardened to: do not ship LEARN_PERSIST=true until step 3 shows in-match signal.

problems.item: "the same window liveTrack uses to aim a gun" (8s)
problems.claim: the kill sweep's `now - r.t > 8` gate is justified as the liveTrack window.
problems.reality: ai.js:1061 is `function liveTrack(r) { return G.time - r.t <= 5; }`. The 8 is a new constant, not an existing one. Harmless numerically, but the rationale's appeal to precedent is false, and this file's standard is that constants cite something real.

problems.item: Exploration is a net in-match cost when the prior is good
problems.claim: "UCB needs nothing... exploration decays because the counts grow".
problems.reality: True but not free. Simulated over 15 waves with a CORRECT prior, mean reward per wave is +0.194 at C=0 and +0.181 at C=0.22 — exploration costs about 0.013 r/wave, roughly 100 credits a wave, and does not pay back inside the match. The payoff exists only where the prior is absent or wrong (flat prior: +0.091 at C=0 vs +0.082 at C=0.22 — still a small cost, because the learning is being bought by the step size, not by the exploration bonus). Worth stating plainly to the owner: within one match this is close to break-even at best.

problems.item: "13 anchored edits" / the prior's existence
problems.claim: summary says 13 edits; priorFor reads a `Doctrine` module.
problems.reality: The edits array contains 14 entries (all 14 anchors verified at count 1 by python str.count — reported in full below). And there is no Doctrine global anywhere in js/ or the HTML harnesses today, so as landed priorFor returns all zeros for every arm: the "pre-trained knowledge" half of the owner's request is delivered entirely by the sibling area, and this loop ships as learn-from-zero. That is safe (index 0 = today's behaviour) but it should be said out loud rather than implied by the cold-start section.

problems.item: "the suite must still be 89/89, and only [29] is at risk"
problems.claim: "They will be, because intel().mix still calls counterMix and counterMix is not edited".
problems.reality: The [29] half is correct and I verified the mechanism: counterMix builds `const inf = {...}` / `const veh = {...}` fresh on every call and returns a new object (ai.js:1576-1577, :1719), so doctrineMix's in-place multiplication cannot leak into intel().mix even though both are evaluated in the same object literal. But the claim that nothing else can move is untested: the tempo arm changes waveT and the launch gate for every commander at Regular and above, and the emph arm changes composition, so any behaviour test that runs a Veteran/Elite commander forward and asserts on wave timing, composition or approach is exposed. Worth confirming that no new G.rng() call was added — correct, the whole block is rng-free, so seeded replays stay deterministic.

missed: Anchor verification (asked for explicitly): all 14 anchors return python str.count == 1 against the current js/ai.js — mineNext:297, reset:429, sighting:936, grave:1177, build-toward comment:1721, counterMix call:3477, reapWave+navalWave:3934, bookWave:4473 (the other bookWave at :4203 does not match the 4-space anchor), score:4344, lastAxes:4527, wave gate:3937, waveT assignment:3938, intel:5422, personalities:5471. Every insert repeats its anchored text, so none of them can produce the `},` `,"dmg"` failure mode.

What the owner will actually SEE, which the design never states: with ~6-8 episodes a match, emph arms worth under one unit of composition each, an axis book that cannot execute two of its three arms, and a tempo book with one broken arm, the visible change is a wave that sometimes leaves early and sometimes leaves late, with a marginally different mix. That is variety. The design's own warning — 'make the commander roll dice among five plans and it will look different every match and play WORSE' — applies to its own emph and axis books as specified.

The build gate interaction is never mentioned: because groundArmy() includes the marching wave, production STOPS entirely while a wave is alive and winning. So the doctrineMix lean is only ever spent on replacing casualties, which means the better a wave does, the less the emphasis arm gets to buy — the arm's influence on the army is inversely proportional to its success. That is a perverse coupling worth designing around (or exploiting: scoring per-purchase rather than per-wave would sidestep it).

Personality mods are not considered: PERSONALITY.turtle sets waveTime 999 and waveSize 30 (ai.js:10), so a Fortress commander launches roughly one wave a match and every book stays on the prior for ever; rusher sets waveTime 55 / waveSize 6, which triples the sample count and makes the books the only commander where learning could actually converge. The loop's sample budget varies by a factor of ~15 across personalities and nothing in the design adapts to that (PRIOR_N and the arm count should scale with expected episodes).

No end-of-match settle: when the commander is defeated or the match ends, the open episode is discarded, so the final and most informative wave of every match is never scored — and with persistence on, the slot is saved from the second-to-last wave's state.

seenU records are hostile-only (noteContact at :880 rejects `e.owner === P || G.allied(P, e.owner)`), which the fog audit does not claim but should: it is what stops an ally's losses near our wave from being booked as our kills in a 3+ player game. Conversely, an enemy killed near our wave by the HUMAN or by a third party is still credited to the wave — the sweep tests proximity, not causation.

A concrete cheaper alternative the design dismisses too fast: one book, not three, over 2-3 arms that actually change the army (e.g. armour-heavy | tube-heavy | infantry-heavy, with the inf:veh split moved), scored per wave. That is 2-3 pulls per arm at 6-8 episodes instead of 1.5-2.5 across ten arms, with effect sizes several times larger — the only configuration in which this reward and this policy have any chance of separating arms inside one match. The 36-arm strawman is not the alternative to three books; two arms in one book is.

Grave-cap arithmetic: the 60-entry cap (:1178) is not the only truncation. graveWeight prunes anything older than min(600, waveTime*3) — 450s at Veteran — and it prunes inside pickApproach, which runs on every launch. Episodes are shorter than that, so the cap is the live risk, and it bites precisely when a 16-24 unit wave is wiped alongside base losses: `lost` silently under-counts and the worst waves report the least punishment.
